name: Venera 1
significance: Venera 1 was humanity's first attempt to reach another planet. Launched by the Soviet Union in February 1961 to strike Venus, it became the first craft to leave Earth on a path to another world. Its radio fell silent after a week, when its Sun-pointing system failed, but before then it returned measurements of the solar wind and interplanetary magnetic field from 1.9 million km out. It drifted past Venus, silent, in May 1961.
statusNote: Launched 1961-02-12 00:34:38 UT on a Molniya (8K78) from Tyuratam (Siddiqi, Beyond Earth). The last good communications session was on 1961-02-17 at 1.9 million km; contact could not be regained on 02-22, after the Sun-orientation system failed. The inert craft passed Venus on 19-20 May 1961 at about 100,000 km and went into solar orbit (Siddiqi). The arrival used here is 1961-05-19. Path calculated: a two-body transfer between the real launch date and the published flyby date. Contact was lost before the flyby, and with no further course changes the craft coasted on that path; no measured trajectory exists, so it is drawn dashed.
